thesis: Somatostatin-expressing interneurons are the inhibitory class most often named as a shared casualty of neurodegeneration, and the claim is built on a genuinely reproducible observation - the somatostatin signal falls - fused to an inference the primary literature has not closed: that the cells themselves are dying. This review separates the two.
scope_notes: Written last (Phase 11) and may cite only papers already used in body sections. It frames SST interneurons as a cell class that is vulnerable across diseases, states the central question, and previews the argument arc.

arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_07.thesis: Interpretation of reporter-based SST cell counts. One study treats reduced eGFP-SST density as a change in the SST population while finding no accompanying death or oxidative-stress signal; the other documents SST-immunonegative tdTomato+ cells in SST-Cre tissue that force exclusion of a whole region from analysis. Together they disagree on whether Cre-reporter density is a valid proxy for SST interneuron number, which is a measurement-validity rather than a biological disagreement.
arg_conflict_cluster_01_conf_07.synthesis: Conflict cluster_01_conf_07 (preview; resolution_status=open). Reporter-based counts versus marker-based counts: introduces the measurement-validity theme that Section 11 resolves. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_02.thesis: Magnitude of SST neuron loss in Alzheimer's disease: stereological counts give a 50% reduction in hippocampus, whereas immunohistochemical counts in cortex find no difference between aged controls and AD. The studies differ in region (hippocampus vs cortex) and in whether design-based stereology was used.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_02.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_02 (preview; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). Stereology in hippocampus versus density counts in cortex give 50% loss versus none. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_05.thesis: Direction of somatostatin change across neurodegenerative diseases: somatostatin content is elevated two- to threefold in Huntington disease basal ganglia, while somatostatin-positive cell density is reduced in Parkinson disease amygdala. Peptide content and cell density are measured by different assays, so the cross-disease contrast may be assay- as well as disease-driven.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_05.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_05 (preview; resolution_status=open). Opposite directions of somatostatin change across diseases measured by different assays; sets up sec-huntingtons and sec-parkinsons-lewy-body. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): measurement_modality_and_what_was_counted.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_07.thesis: Whether amyloid pathology causes loss of hippocampal somatostatin interneurons or only functional impairment of a numerically intact population. The overexpression model reports dysfunction of O-LM interneurons, while the knock-in model finds unchanged SOM interneuron density even at 24 months.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_07.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_07 (preview; resolution_status=open). Overexpression model reports O-LM dysfunction while knock-in reports unchanged density at 24 months; previews the construct-dosage theme. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): model_construct_and_species_transfer.

arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_09.thesis: Whether traumatic brain injury produces a consistent, quantifiable depletion of somatostatin interneurons. Controlled cortical impact yields significant ipsilateral SST interneuron loss and afferent disconnection, whereas lateral fluid percussion injury yields heterogeneous hippocampal changes and no obvious cortical interneuron loss.
arg_conflict_cluster_02_conf_09.synthesis: Conflict cluster_02_conf_09 (preview; resolution_status=resolved-by-method). Two TBI models disagree on whether SST depletion is consistent and quantifiable. Primary axis (rule-derived, provisional): species_region_and_circuit_context.

arg_unanchored.thesis: Somatostatin-expressing interneurons are the inhibitory class most often named as a shared casualty of neurodegeneration, and the claim is built on a genuinely reproducible observation - the somatostatin signal falls - fused to an inference the primary literature has not closed: that the cells themselves are dying. This review separates the two.
arg_unanchored.synthesis: 23 of 28 papers in this package are not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict. They are the synthesis density of the section: group them into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each, giving landmark papers (argument_role=landmark) detailed treatment and the rest integrated as converging evidence. Do not cover them sequentially.

opening_constraint: Document opening (no preceding section). Open on the review's own question: Is loss or dysfunction of somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons a shared, causally important feature across neurodegenerative diseases? If so, which mechanisms (cell-intrinsic vulnerability, peptide/SSTR signaling, circuit dysregulation) drive it, how robust is the human and model evidence, and does it justify SST-targeted biomarkers and therapies? Frame SST interneurons as a cell class reported vulnerable across diseases, state the central question, and preview the three-act arc; cite only papers already used in body sections.
closing_constraint: Ends by stating that evaluating any disease claim requires first fixing what an SST interneuron is and what the somatostatin signal measures, which is the task of (sec-sst-identity).
framing_limits: Must not claim exhaustive coverage; states database scope and absence of citation chasing.
Must not preview a conclusion stronger than Section 12 delivers.

certified_evidence_limits.search_coverage: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval. Endpoints actually used: Europe PMC REST search (resultType=core) and fullTextXML, NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc), CrossRef. No other database contributed a comparable share, so coverage claims must be scoped to these sources.
certified_evidence_limits.citation_chasing: None. No backward or forward citation chasing was performed. No section may claim completeness of coverage; write 'no study examining X was retrieved by these searches', never 'no study has examined X'.
certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. Sections whose argument rests on that literature must state the asymmetry in the section body, not only in Methods.
certified_evidence_limits.disconfirming_sweeps: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. Negative-result and conflict coverage is a top-relevance sample, not a census. Report null results as 'reported null results include ...'; never as 'no contradicting evidence exists'. No rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_axis_labels_provisional: Axes were assigned by a documented rule applied to the recorded nature_of_conflict text. Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_inventory_caveat: This inventory is the set of disagreements recorded during a search whose disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. It is a top-relevance sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and no rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval with no citation chasing (snowball_rounds = 0)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: No section may claim completeness of coverage. The Methods section states the database scope and the absence of backward/forward citation chasing explicitly. Claims of the form "no study has examined X" are written as "no study examining X was retrieved by these searches", and every such statement in a body section is sourced to a recorded evidence gap rather than asserted.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Full-text share varies from 77/77 (circuits, cluster_07) to 22/87 (human evidence, cluster_08) because the older postmortem and CSF literature is closed-access
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 9 is the section whose underlying literature is least directly verified. Its thesis is written so that the central synthesis rests on the modern open-access single-nucleus cohorts, with the 1980s radioimmunoassay series treated as a historically important but abstract-level record; the asymmetry is stated in the section itself, not buried in Methods. Section 5 (25/80 full text) carries the same caveat for its historical CSF series.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query, so negative-result coverage is a top-relevance sample rather than an exhaustive search
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Null results are reported as "reported null results include ..." and never as "no contradicting evidence exists". Section 11 states that the conflict inventory is a sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and that the true rate of unreplicated or contradicted claims is bounded below by what is recorded here.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: cluster_09's replication ceiling (therapeutics) is met by a single enabling label; 60 of 86 findings are replication_unknown
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 10 is framed as an assessment of translational status, not of efficacy. No therapeutic claim in that section may be described as replicated unless the specific replicating DOI is named, and the section foregrounds that much of the SSTR4 evidence base comes from one closely related research programme.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Figure comparisons are heterogeneous: no figure_data entry is uniform on all four homogeneity_check fields
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Every figure specification states the heterogeneity it must display rather than smooth, and the document-level figure rules forbid pooled summaries outright.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Several prominent mechanistic claims are flagged as false-consensus risks in the evidence record (metabolic load as the cause of SST vulnerability; SST/GABA co-transmission; absolute sparing of striatal interneurons in HD)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Each is introduced in prose as a widely repeated claim whose primary demonstration was not retrieved, in sections 3, 2 and 6 respectively, and each is listed in the section 11 open-questions inventory.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Introduce the measurement problem: in most of this literature the cell is identified by the molecule being measured. Preview the four axes along which the literature disagrees (measurement modality, region, model construct, cohort co-pathology).

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: The central question and the structure of the argument
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: State the thesis question verbatim in scientific form, then lay out the three-act arc and what each section contributes, with forward cross-references.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Scope, evidence base and what this review does not cover
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: State the database scope and absence of citation chasing, the varying depth of full-text access across the disease literatures, and the deliberate exclusion of non-neurodegenerative psychiatric somatostatin literature except where it bears on specificity.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Interpretation of reporter-based SST cell counts. One study treats reduced eGFP-SST density as a change in the SST population while finding no accompanying death or oxidative-stress signal; the other documents SST-immunonegative tdTomato+ cells in SST-Cre tissue that force exclusion of a whole region from analysis. Together they disagree on whether Cre-reporter density is a valid proxy for SST interneuron number, which is a measurement-validity rather than a biological disagreement.

Magnitude of SST neuron loss in Alzheimer's disease: stereological counts give a 50% reduction in hippocampus, whereas immunohistochemical counts in cortex find no difference between aged controls and AD. The studies differ in region (hippocampus vs cortex) and in whether design-based stereology was used.

Direction of somatostatin change across neurodegenerative diseases: somatostatin content is elevated two- to threefold in Huntington disease basal ganglia, while somatostatin-positive cell density is reduced in Parkinson disease amygdala. Peptide content and cell density are measured by different assays, so the cross-disease contrast may be assay- as well as disease-driven.

Whether amyloid pathology causes loss of hippocampal somatostatin interneurons or only functional impairment of a numerically intact population. The overexpression model reports dysfunction of O-LM interneurons, while the knock-in model finds unchanged SOM interneuron density even at 24 months.

Whether traumatic brain injury produces a consistent, quantifiable depletion of somatostatin interneurons. Controlled cortical impact yields significant ipsilateral SST interneuron loss and afferent disconnection, whereas lateral fluid percussion injury yields heterogeneous hippocampal changes and no obvious cortical interneuron loss.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict; group into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each rather than covering sequentially.

curation_notes.assignment_rule: Deterministic cluster->section mapping from gate_scope.json cluster_to_section_assignment, applied to unique (doi, claim_source_sentence) evidence units.
curation_notes.bookend_rule: Sections 01 and 12 are bookends written at Phase 11 and may cite only papers already used in body sections. Each bookend finding is a Phase 2 finding whose DOI also carries a different finding, with a different claim_source_sentence, in a body section - so the paper is already in the body and the two sections quote different sentences.
curation_notes.duplicate_policy: 35 of 844 Phase 2 findings were byte-identical (same DOI and same claim_source_sentence) records of the same observation in two or more clusters. They were merged into the surviving finding object (also_recorded_in_clusters / duplicate_finding_ids_merged) and logged in unassigned_findings.json; none were deleted.
curation_notes.conflict_axis_caveat: AXIS labels on conflicts are rule-derived and provisional (scaffold conflict_coverage.axis_assignment_method). Correct any tag that misreads a conflict.
curation_notes.citation_discipline: Papers in this package come only from Phase 2 outputs. Do not introduce new citations; cite_keys are from the certified citation_key_map and author names only from author_name_table.
